title: the Glass Steppe Rising Anew
premise: Rosalind Whitlock, exiled to the magicless valley of Greyhollow for a storm-calling that killed a king's heir, has lived twelve years as a nameless farrier. When the old gods stir beneath the Glass Steppe and begin answering prayers again, his buried power wakes with them—and with it the attention of the court beneath the mountain, which holds the soul of his sister Wren, sold to pay his exile's blood-price. Guided by a disgraced paladin of the moon-cult and a god who answers through crows, Rosalind must cross the Steppe, outwit the Undercourt's bargains, and steal Wren's soul back before the thirteenth moon turns. He succeeds only by surrendering his own name to the gods in exchange—yet in giving it up, he finally finds the belonging exile denied him, returning to Greyhollow not as a fugitive but as its chosen guardian.
about_author: Beatrix Zhou is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent a decade transcribing small-town disputes before turning them into epics. She writes fantasy about people the law forgot, from a farmhouse full of rescued crows.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Establishes Greyhollow's magicless quiet, Rosalind's careful anonymity as a farrier, and the ritual he performs each dawn to keep his storm-blood dormant. Emotional beat: weary vigilance, the ache of a life half-lived.

chapters.title: A Prayer in the Smokehouse
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A dying neighbor prays aloud to the old gods—and something answers. The candles gutter, frost blooms, and Rosalind feels his power stir for the first time in twelve years. Beat: dread and forbidden hope.

chapters.title: The Crow That Knew My Name
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A crow with a human eye delivers a message in his childhood nickname—known only to his sold sister, Wren. Beat: shock cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, with a flashback to the night of the storm that killed the king's heir and Wren's bargain with the Undercourt. He learns the moon's thirteenth turn seals her soul forever. Beat: guilt transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: The Paladin of the Broken Order
chapters.summary: Sera Vane's POV. A disgraced moon-paladin arrives in Greyhollow hunting the 'storm-witch' of the old rumors. She finds a tired farrier instead—and recognizes the gods' fingerprints on him. Beat: wary mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: An Arrest That Isn't
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera chooses not to report Rosalind, violating her oath, and instead demands he help her investigate why the gods are waking. Beat: the first fracture in her duty.

chapters.title: What the Gods Want
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Through the crow-god Corvass, they learn the old gods wake because the Undercourt has been hoarding mortal souls—including Wren's—as currency. Beat: the quest takes shape.

chapters.title: Leaving Greyhollow
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. He crosses the valley's boundary; magic floods back like cold water, and his storms crackle under his skin. The valley's elders brand him traitor. Beat: terror and exhilaration of becoming himself.

chapters.title: The Glass Steppe
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Vast, mirror-flat, and haunted by reflections that move independently. The party is stalked by a reflection-Rosalind who still serves the court. Beat: isolation and self-confrontation.

chapters.title: The Reflection Bargain
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The mirror-self offers Rosalind his old life back if he abandons Wren. Sera argues him away from it, revealing her own broken vow. Beat: reluctant trust kindling.

chapters.title: Salt and Lanterns
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The border town of Saltmere, where the moon-cult's remnants hide. They learn the Undercourt opens only to those carrying a debt freely owed. Beat: camaraderie, first laughter on the road.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. An Undercourt agent offers to forgive Sera's disgrace if she delivers Rosalind. She refuses—but doesn't tell him. Beat: secret guilt planted.

chapters.title: Storms Remembered
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. His power surges uncontrollably near the Steppe's storm-wells; Sera's moon-blessing anchors him, and they share the truth of their pasts by firelight. Beat: intimacy against duty.

chapters.title: The God of Small Prayers
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Corvass reveals the gods wake because prayers need a debtor—and Rosalind's exile made him the perfect conduit. Beat: the personal cost of cosmic design.

chapters.title: The Moon's Twelfth Waning
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The deadline looms: one moon left. The Undercourt's gates will seal at the thirteenth turn. Beat: ticking-clock urgency.

chapters.title: The Hollow King's Road
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They travel the corpse-road of a dead god, beset by soul-wraiths. Rosalind learns to command storms not as a weapon but as shelter. Beat: mastery earned through mercy.

chapters.title: What Sera Buried
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Flashback: Sera's order fell because she refused to burn a village of god-touched children. Her disgrace was her righteousness. Beat: her honor reframed.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A bridge-warden demands a name as toll. Rosalind gives a false one—and the bridge rejects it, forcing him to speak his true name aloud for the first time in twelve years. Beat: identity as currency.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They reach the Undercourt's obsidian gates, where the debt must be freely offered. Rosalind pledges his service. Beat: crossing the threshold, no way back.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Souls
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Inside the court: a bureaucracy of the damned. They locate Wren's soul in the Ledger of Forfeit, held as collateral against Rosalind's exile-price. Beat: hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: The Understeward's Offer
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The Understeward offers Wren's freedom for Rosalind's soul instead—the original debt, plus interest. Beat: temptation to self-sacrifice as easy answer.

chapters.title: Wren, Unbodied
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (dream-contact through the crow-god). Wren's soul, twelve years in the court's vaults, has learned its secrets—including that the court fears the waking gods. Beat: the rescued becomes the guide.

chapters.title: A Bargain Poorly Read
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind nearly signs the exchange, but Wren's dream-warning reveals a clause: his soul would fuel the court's war on the gods. Beat: betrayal averted by sisterhood.

chapters.title: The Court Declares Hunt
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Their deception discovered, the party flees through the court's shifting halls as the Hunt is called. Beat: pure pursuit, adrenaline.

chapters.title: The Moon Turns Thirteenth
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The deadline passes at the gates as they escape—but Wren's soul, forewarned, slipped its ledger into Rosalind's storm-mark during the dream. Beat: the deadline broken by cunning, not force.

chapters.title: Above the Mountain
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They emerge into a snowstorm with Wren's soul hidden in Rosalind's scars—but the court's hunters follow, and the sky itself turns against them. Beat: breathless escape, fragile victory.

chapters.title: The Hunt on the Glass
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The Hunt corners them on the Steppe. Sera holds the line alone, spending her moon-blessing to buy Rosalind time. Beat: sacrifice as love's proof.

chapters.title: What Sera Paid
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Drained and mortal, Sera confesses the Debt Collector's offer she once refused—and why refusing cost her everything. Rosalind forgives her. Beat: honesty as the true vow.

chapters.title: Corvass's Price
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The crow-god offers to shield Wren's soul from recall—for a price: Rosalind's name, surrendered to the gods, making him their vessel. Beat: the cost of belonging.

chapters.title: The Recall
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The Undercourt's last hunter invokes the original contract to drag Wren's soul back. Rosalind must choose now: sign the surrender or lose her forever. Beat: the decision point.

chapters.title: The Name Given
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. He speaks his true name into the storm and lets the gods take it—becoming the storm itself. The hunter is unmade; Wren's soul is freed into a body of rain and light. Beat: transcendence through loss.

chapters.title: The Storm That Chose
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Reborn, Wren searches the wreckage for her brother and finds only weather that answers when she speaks. Beat: grief and wonder intertwined.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain Falls
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. With its chief hunter destroyed and the gods awake, the Undercourt's ledger-crats flee; the hoarded souls rise like embers and return to their waiting bodies across the land. Beat: cathartic, world-changing release.

chapters.title: Learning to Speak Weather
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and the nameless storm-being learn to communicate—grief, jokes, old lullabies carried in wind and thunder. Beat: love outlasting identity.

chapters.title: The Return to Greyhollow
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera leads Wren home, where the valley elders must reckon with the storm-guardian they exiled. The gods offer Greyhollow a covenant. Beat: homecoming with terms.

chapters.title: A Guardian, Not a Prisoner
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV (as the storm). Offered restoration of his name and human form, Rosalind chooses instead to remain the valley's weather—free, bound to no court, god, or law. Beat: belonging redefined.

chapters.title: Sera's New Oath
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera refounds the moon-cult in Greyhollow as an order of covenant-keepers, serving neither crown nor court. Beat: duty rebuilt from love.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon, Full
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the anniversary, the valley celebrates the Night of Returned Souls. Wren dances in the rain that answers her laughter. Beat: joy earned.

chapters.title: What the Crows Remember
chapters.summary: Corvass's POV. The crow-god reflects: gods are made of surrendered names, and Rosalind's was the finest gift. He keeps a feather of the storm in his nest. Beat: myth-making, the story becoming legend.

chapters.title: Rising Anew
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Years later: Greyhollow thrives under its storm-guardian, Wren teaches the god-touched children, and Sera's order grows. On quiet evenings, the rain taps the farrier's old forge like a knock from a friend come home. Beat: peace, belonging, and love that outlasted every law.
